Team — forwarding a customer issue that just came up 1 hour before our demo. Finsight's Exchange/Google mix is stripping the DESCRIPTION field (they say the join link disappears). Their tenant also blocks organizer transfer which prevents our usual Organizer->Guest fallback.

Can Ops/Platform please:
- Confirm if the invite we sent had the join link in the DESCRIPTION and SUMMARY fields of the .ics. (I attached the original invite to this thread as an .ics stub.)
- If SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION were truncated, can we quickly regenerate an .ics that includes the join URL in the DESCRIPTION and as a top-line clickable link in the event body so their clients see it?
- If a bridge is needed, can Marcus provision a temporary Zoom fallback (bridge) and send a new invite?

Attachments: invite-original.ics (attached by sender)

This is high-urgency — customer waiting in the meeting room. If we can't guarantee their calendar will show a clickable join link, we'll need to DM them a direct URL and update the invite.

Thanks — K

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Alex — calendar description truncated, guest can't join

Kim — saw this. Quick notes after checking the outgoing invite headers:
- The invite did contain the full join URL in DESCRIPTION and in X-ALT-DESC; however, Exchange servers occasionally drop long DESCRIPTION fields when organizer is external to the tenant.
- Short-term mitigation: regenerate an .ics with a condensed DESCRIPTION (first line contains explicit "Join: https://zoom.us/j/XXXX"), and place the full URL in the SUMMARY and in the top of the HTML body too. That increases the chance the URL survives server-side truncation.
- Marcus can provision a temporary Zoom bridge (we have a pool) and provide a direct meeting URL within 10 minutes.

Marcus — can you spin a bridge and reply with the link? Priyom, FYI on calendar resource/organizer transfer constraints — we should log this as an item for the calendar-compatibility playbook.

— Ben
Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
